L25: Dom Milano is entering his third season with the Harper Hawks as head coach in 2026. His assistant coaches this year are 【5†Mason】 【5†Schaller】 and 【6†Hank】 【6†Schau】, both entering their third season. Schaller is the assistant to the head coach while Schau is the head pitching coach
L26: Milano took over the team in 2024 with an interim tag. In 2025, the Hawks transitioned to NJCAA DII as Milano led the Hawks to their best record in over 25 years with 36 wins on the field.

L50: Before Harper
L51: Milano went to his first baseball game when he was eight years old. His father has been the coach of 【9†Nazareth†www.nazarethacademy.com】 for 25+ years. He went on to play there as well and his senior year the team finished third in the state while he ended his high school career with an All-State nomination, a First Team All-Area nomination, a Honorable Mention All-Area nomination, and two All-Conference nominations.
L52: Milano played collegiately as well. He started out at Triton, playing for two seasons. In his first season, his season was cut short due to a UCL tear that required Tommy John surgery. His second season was also cut short, this time due to Covid. After a rough two seasons at Triton, Milano decided to transfer to Morton. He was an integral part in changing their program as the 【11†Panthers†gomcpanthers.com】 made the NJCAA DII Region IV playoffs. Milano average .322 with an OPS of 1.067.
L53: He led the country in walks, was 4th in triples, and 42nd in stolen bases. His play earned him a scholarship opportunity to play for 【10†Butler†butlersports.com】.
L54: At 【10†Butler†butlersports.com】 he played in 71 games. During his senior year, he played for legendary coach Dave Schrage who had 804 wins at the DI level. He hit .390 in the Big East and earned Conference Weekly Honor Roll the week of April 11th, 2023. During his senior year Milano played for Blake Beemer who was the youngest head coach in the country at the time of his hire.
L55: Milano's coaching career started when he was only 16 years old with Illinois Premier. Since 2019, he has been coaching for the 【8†Cangelosi Sparks North†bjesbensenville.com】. Milano also volunteer coaches at 【9†Nazareth†www.nazarethacademy.com】 in his spare time under his father. 【9†Nazareth†www.nazarethacademy.com】 won state championships in 2022 and 2023 in which Milano helped with scouting and game planning.
L56: Coach Milano is currently a coach at the 【12†Bo Jackson Dome†bjesbensenville.com】 in Bensenville. He is the head coach of 【8†Cangelosi Sparks North†bjesbensenville.com】, one of the top five travel organizations in the state of Illinois in 2024.

L7: # Hawks Ready to Take Flight in 2026
L8: 
L9: 【4†Image: Baseball Team (2026)†images.sidearmdev.com】
L10: 
L11: Michael Hubatch
L12: 
L13: Men's Baseball | 2/9/2026 11:19:00 AM
L14: Palatine, IL: The baseball season is right around the corner as the Hawks come into the season with the highest expectations ever going into a season. Coach 【5†Dominic Milano】 will enter his second season as head coach without the interim tag. He will be assisted by third year pitching coach, 【6†Hank Schau】 and third year assistant coach, 【7†Mason Schaller】.
L15: Last year's Hawks team arguably had the most successful season in the last 30 years. On the field, the Hawks were 36-15, and finished losing in the Sectional Championship to #9 Kankakee 8-7. Last year's team saw over 10 players move on to the 4 year level, including 【8†Dominic Jacoby】 to Louisville University.
L16: This year's roster will feature 29 returning players from last year's team. The Hawks return six players offensively who all had over 100 PAs and hit over .325, and return six out of their top eight arms in terms of innings pitched. Coach 【5†Milano】 is extremely excited about the familiarity, "Returning so many players who contributed at a high level is a blessing. Familiarity with how we want to play, and how we want to practice and prepare everyday goes a long way towards success."
L17: The Hawks have 11 new players that they are excited about as well. That features a mix of transfers and freshmen. "We were really picky about the guys we were bringing into this class due to so many returning players, but we are really high on the group of new guys and expect several to contribute at a high level."
L18: Here is a breakdown of the 2026 Hawks by position:
L19: Catching
L20: The Hawks have three faces back from last year's catching staff. 【9†Kevin Geake】 caught over 70 percent of the innings last year, threw out 16 runners, and had a .330 AVG. 【10†Matt Guza】 returns after having a productive spring and fall. He slashed .360 AVG last spring in 35 PAs. 【10†Guza】 committed to continue his baseball and academic career at Judson University. The last returner is 【11†Gustavo Vivas】, who will fight for time.
L21: The new face in the catching room is 【12†Collin Roche】, who is a two time state champion out of Nazareth Academy. 【12†Roche】 exceeded expectations this fall and has put himself in a position to fight for a lot of playing time.
L22: Infield
L23: One of the strongest areas on the field for the Hawks will be the infield play. Returning close to 500 PAs between 【13†Nick Drtina】 (Purdue Commit), 【14†Michael Mango】, and 【15†Alex Tabbert】. 【13†Drtina】 committed to Purdue University this fall, after slashing .407/514/.568 as a freshman. 【14†Mango】 and 【15†Tabbert】 each had successful seasons as well. 【14†Mango】 hit .359 AVG with an .OPS of .927 and 18 SB. 【15†Tabbert】 hit .351 with a team high 27 SB.
L24: Some new faces in the Hawk Infield include former Eastern Michigan Commit, 【16†Aiden Nohava】, from Brother Rice HS, 【17†Cooper Nelson】 from Fremd HS, 【18†Griffin Kelly】 from Buffalo Grove HS and 【19†Lewis Barbour】 from IC Catholic HS. 【16†Nohava】 possesses a loud bat from the right side, 【17†Nelson】 possesses elite athleticism and quick twitch, 【18†Kelly】 possesses a strong approach with some juice from the left side, and 【19†Barbour】 possesses a ton of versatility and high Baseball IQ.
L25: A returner fighting for time is 【20†Jaxon Cook】. As a freshman in 16 ABs, 【20†Cook】 hit .375. 【20†Cook】 recently committed to play baseball at Eureka College the next two years.
L26: The rest of the infield is rounded out by returners 【21†Evan Fahey】, and 【22†Jay Younan】.
L27: Outfield
L28: The outfield, much like the rest of the position groups, returns a solid foundation. It is headlined by 【23†Connor Kave】 and 【24†Brayden Clancy】. As a freshman 【23†Kave】 played stellar defense, and slashed .327 with 21 SBs. 【24†Clancy】, arguably the Hawks most valuable player, slashed .363 with an OPS of 1.056 and proved to play almost everywhere on the diamond.
L29: Also returning in the outfield are sophomores 【25†Will Hickey】, 【26†Peter Castaneda】, and 【27†Brandon Koth】. All four look to take a jump in their roles from last year. Look for 【25†Hickey】 to step into a lot more time after a really productive fall.
L30: The Hawks outfield is rounded out by 【28†Owen Anderson】. Some other players that could see time in the outfield include previously mentioned 【19†Lewis Barbour】, 【16†Aiden Nohava】, 【12†Collin Roche】, and 【15†Alex Tabbert】.
L31: Designated Hitter
L32: The designated hitter role is almost like a power play card for this Hawks team. It can be filled by about anyone on the roster and will be rotated between several players throughout the year.
L33: Pitching
L34: Pitching is another huge area where the Hawks saw a ton of improvement from 2024 to 2025 under Coach 【6†Schau】. The Hawks ERA went from 10.26 to 5.46, and the staff this year will look to improve on that even more. The Hawks have 20 arms on the roster, between returners and new players.
L35: The Hawks return several high profile arms. 【29†Logan Sarna】, who recently committed to Nationally ranked DII Grand Valley State, returns after throwing 47 ⅓ IP, with a 2.47 ERA and a .201 BAA. He will look to take another step forward. The Hawks also return Second Team All-Region Selection (2024) in 【30†Mason Hulligan】. 【30†Hulligan】 looks to have a great year after coming off of injury. The Hawks also return sophomores 【31†Zach Zalewski】, 【32†David Essien】, and 【21†Evan Fahey】.
L36: All three threw over 18 innings as freshman. 【32†Essien】 looks to take a huge step forward after now improving his velocity to 96 MPH.
L37: The Hawks also bring back 【33†Zack LaBrec】 (Judson Commit), 【34†Jeremy Florez】, 【22†Younan】, 【35†Anthony Santos】, and 【36†Braylon Singer】.
L38: On top of all those returners, the coaching staff is extremely excited about the new arms the Hawks acquired. There are several impact transfers expected to contribute. Those include redshirt freshmen 【37†Kenny Nanos】 from Valparaiso University and 【38†Cal Korosa】 from McHenry County. Along with the transfers, there are several freshmen looking to carve out big roles. Those include RHP 【39†Gavin O'Neil】, and LHPs 【18†Griffin Kelly】 and 【40†Riley Blackwell】.
L39: All three freshmen are competing for spots in the starting rotation.
L40: Other new faces that are competing for time on the mound include 【41†Jonah Elvidge】 and 【42†Daniel Gross】.
L41: Season Starts South
L42: The Hawks kick off their season on February 13th against three NJCAA DI schools. The season opens with four games in three days against 【43†Saint Charles†www.sccathletics.com】, followed by a round robin with 【44†Jefferson College†www.jeffco.edu】 and 【45†Kansas City Community College†bluedevils.kckcc.edu】.
L43: The following weekend the Hawks will travel to Heartland's Corn Crib to play perineal powerhouses 【46†Kirkwood†www.kirkwoodeagles.com】, 【47†Parkland†athletics.parkland.edu】, and 【48†Lincoln Land†lincolnlandloggers.com】.
L44: "We set up our schedule to play some bigger nationally known JUCOs early on. It does not matter what you do in February and early March. Region play is what matters the most. Playing this difficult schedule early on will prepare us for Region play." stated Coach 【5†Milano】.
L45: Eyes on Enid
L46: With a deep roster, proven leadership, and plenty of motivation, the Hawks head into 2026 ready to build on last year's success. The mix of experienced returners and talented newcomers gives Coach 【5†Milano】 and his staff one of the most balanced Harper lineups in his lifetime, one that can compete with anyone in Region 4.
L47: After coming within striking distance of a regional title last spring, the Hawks are determined to finish what they started. Their experience, chemistry, and hunger set the tone for a season defined by high standards and higher aspirations. The path won't be easy, but this group has embraced the challenge. Their sights are firmly set on Enid, Oklahoma, and a run at the NJCAA Division II World Series.

L219: Expressive Activity & Free Expression Zones
L220: The United States and Minnesota Constitutions’ guarantee all individuals the right to the freedom of expression. In recognition of its status as a public institution of higher learning, Minnesota North College at the Itasca Campus, identifies the area in front of the entrance to Backes Hall as the area open to the public for the free expression of ideas during the hours of 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. without prior approval and without the requirement of a use agreement or fee.
L221: Any and all related activities cannot impede individuals from coming or going through this area, in other words a reasonable walk- though path must be maintained at all times.
L222: In most cases, it is preferable for an individual or group, be they a Minnesota North College affiliated or not, to follow the scheduling procedures identified in this Policy to ensure the free expression zone is available at a time when an individual or group wish to make use of it. Moreover, scheduled use of a free expression zone supersedes any unscheduled use of the property.
L223: Nevertheless, subject to reasonable time, place and manner restrictions, an individual or group may make use of a free expression zone when otherwise not in use or scheduled for use by another individual or group. Minnesota North College encourages the college community to be tolerant of those exposing different points of view while taking advantage of the opportunities to express themselves and be exposed to new ideas.
L224: All other areas indoors and outdoors must follow the college reservation approval process including facility use agreements or fees as appropriate.
